buyer_reported_costs.finding: A 12-employee law firm paid $3,500 one-time setup plus $350/month for a custom website chatbot with CRM (Clio) and Calendly integration; the case study claims $25,200/year in labor and missed-lead savings.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Vendor case study published by the agency (Streamline IQ); vendor-reported ROI, not verified

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Four small-business AI agent builds were sold for $1,650, $4,000, $6,000 and $12,000 - $23,000 total - for an outreach agent, a sales/CRM agent, an internal Slack assistant and a member-facing 'AI concierge'.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Third-party write-up of one automation team's four projects; seller-side pricing, buyers' identities and outcomes not disclosed

buyer_reported_costs.finding: Among 30 agencies that publish a monthly fee and no one-time price, the median retainer is $5,000/mo, ranging $2,000-$15,000/mo; among 140 agencies publishing a one-time entry price, the median is $2,000 and 99 of 140 start below $5,000.
buyer_reported_costs.context: AgenticIndex statistical report over 290 indexed agencies, 205 of which publish prices; these are published list prices, not invoices

buyer_reported_costs.finding: An AI automation agency profile on Clutch shows an average hourly rate of $100-$149/hour, a $10,000+ minimum project size, and a most common project size of $10,000-$49,999 (from 5 of 8 reviews).
buyer_reported_costs.context: Third-party directory metadata (Clutch listing for 'AI Automation Agency 360'); the profile page itself returned HTTP 403 so the figures come from the listing as surfaced in search results

buyer_reported_costs.finding: US automation freelancers on Upwork advertise a median $80/hr, with the middle half at $60-$120/hr, the bottom tenth at $45/hr or less and the top tenth at $175/hr+; the worldwide median for the same category is $35/hr.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Independent index of 114 public Upwork profiles with $10K+ earnings; advertised rates, before Upwork's client marketplace fee

what_is_included_vs_extra.point: The build fee usually buys the build only. Tool, hosting and model-usage bills sit on the client's own accounts and are excluded - TwoCore puts them at $20-$150/month at cost, AutomateNexus at $30-$150/month, and SuperDupr estimates about $114/month for a receptionist at 400 calls of 3 minutes.

Paid discovery is commonly credited against the build: Automaly's assessment (from $6,500) is credited in full, NJ AI Automation credits its $500 audit, OVAMIND takes $500 off the sprint, and Agentomte credits its $1,900 audit.

Post-launch fix windows differ sharply and are the cheapest thing to get wrong: 14 days (OVAMIND sprint), 30 days (TwoCore, HA Technologies, Agentomte handover docs), 30-90 days (NJ AI Automation), 2 weeks (MapScale Automation Setup), 90 days on Nyza's top tier.
A retainer normally buys monitoring plus small changes; without it every tweak becomes a new scope and a new invoice, and nothing is watching for silent failures when an API or CRM field changes.
Voice agents are metered: Dominion's $297/month includes 500 minutes then 25 cents a minute; LuMay's $249/$499/$999 plans include 500/1,000/2,000 minutes at $0.23/$0.22/$0.21 per overage minute.

Setup, training and support are sometimes bundled at the low end - Dominion states all three are included in every package and adds no setup fee - but the same page declines to publish contract, trial, refund or cancellation terms.

Annual billing is where the discount lives at the productised end: LuMay says annual billing saves the equivalent of two months versus monthly, and its cloud and on-prem tiers are annual subscriptions.

Ownership and exit terms are a real differentiator worth pricing: TwoCore lets the client cancel with 30 days notice and keep the build; Agentomte hands over repos, data and keys with no lock-in; Nyza transfers code and credentials on delivery.

What money does not buy at the cheap end, stated by the vendor itself: no promised setup time, no guaranteed number of calls, leads or bookings, and no connection to existing booking/practice software until confirmed.

buyer_complaints.complaint: Skepticism that 'AI automation agency' offers are mostly template resells: an n8n community thread titled around agencies feeling like a scam questions whether buyers get custom work or a generic package.

Fragility and monitoring gaps: an agency owner's public post-mortem describes losing a $2,500/month client after a lead-capture automation ran broken for three days and roughly 40 leads were missed - a recurring theme in buyer complaints about cheap builds.

Mis-set expectations on what a build fee covers: buyers are surprised that model, hosting and CRM subscription costs continue after the project ends, which several agencies now pre-empt by publishing running-cost estimates.
Price opacity itself: most agencies quote only after a sales call, which buyers and even competing agencies flag as making two quotes impossible to compare on scope.

price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: $99-$1,999 one-time for a single build, plus $49-$199/mo care plans (Nyza); $297-$597/mo all-in productised packages with 500 voice minutes (Dominion); $97-$250/hr offshore and mid-market freelancers on Upwork (worldwide median $35/hr)
price_ranges.mid_market: $1,500-$7,500 one-time per workflow or single agent (TwoCore, NJ AI Automation, AI Strike Force, HA Technologies, AutomateNexus, Nyza Pro), with retainers of $250-$2,500/mo (NJ AI Automation, TwoCore, AgenticIndex category medians $800-$4,500 entry)
price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: $10,000-$75,000 projects and $2,500-$10,000+/mo retainers (SuperDupr, LuMay, Automaly, Agentomte, OVAMIND, HA Technologies, AgenticIndex retainer-only median $5,000/mo); $125-$250+/hr for senior US build work
price_ranges.inference_note: Ranges are the overlap of individually cited published prices, not averages I calculated from an invoice dataset. The low band is set by the cheapest published complete offer (Nyza $99-$1,999 builds, $49-$199/mo care) and the Upwork worldwide median; the mid band by the cluster of US one-workflow prices ($1,500-$7,500) and small-business retainers ($250-$2,500); the high band by published multi-agent/pilot/pod prices and the $5,000 median of 30 retainer-only agencies in AgenticIndex's 2026 report. Where a vendor publishes only a range, the range is reproduced as published.

implications_for_consultancy: [Inference] The contested, price-anchored tier for a 5-200 staff Middlesex County client is the one-workflow build at $1,500-$5,000 plus $250-$1,000/mo. Reasoning: two of the closest local comparables publish exactly that (NJ AI Automation: $1,500-$5,000 implementation, $250-$1,000/mo support; TwoCore: $1,500-$5,000 per workflow, $500-$1,500/mo), and the cheapest credible US builds cluster there. A consultancy priced above $5,000 for a first workflow has to justify it with integration depth, not with 'AI'.

[Inference] Buyers in this segment already accept a paid, credited audit at $497-$1,900. Reasoning: MapScale $497, NJ AI Automation $500 (credited), AI Strike Force's audit-inclusive entry, OVAMIND $500 strategy call, Agentomte $1,900, HA Technologies $1,200, Automaly $6,500. A $750-$1,500 assessment credited against the build sits inside the accepted band and de-risks the client's first cheque.

[Inference] The weakest-defended price point is the $297-$600/mo 'AI receptionist/automation' package. Reasoning: Dominion sells $597/mo with setup and voice minutes included, and Nyza sells $99-$799 builds with $49-$199/mo care. Competing there as a local consultant means competing with a productised build; better to position the monthly retainer at $750-$2,500 with named hours, monitoring and a quarterly review, where NJ AI Automation ($250-$1,000), TwoCore ($500-$1,500) and AgenticIndex's fractional-advisory median ($3,500/mo) leave room.

[Inference] A higher price is defensible when the deliverable is integration and continuity, not the agent. Reasoning: every vendor that publishes exclusions points at the same gaps - tool/API costs on the client's accounts ($20-$150/mo), no guaranteed call volumes, no connection to practice/booking software until confirmed, and silent failures when a vendor changes an API. A local firm that owns those gaps (accounts in the client's name, monitoring with response times, documented handover) is selling what the cheap tier explicitly excludes.

[Inference] Hourly work is a weak headline but a useful change-order rate. Reasoning: US automation freelancers advertise a median $80/hr and $60-$120 middle band on Upwork, NJ-serving The Automators publishes $125/hr, OVAMIND lists $250/hr (launch price) and XRAY $250/hr in 4/10/20-hour blocks. A local rate of $125-$175/hr is inside the market; quoting a fixed price first matches how nearly all published US offers are structured.

[Inference] Retainers above ~$2,500/mo put the firm in a different buying conversation. Reasoning: AgenticIndex's retainer-only cohort (30 agencies) medians $5,000/mo, and the fractional/embedded offers (LuMay pod $35K-$75K/mo, OVAMIND $10,000/mo, HA Technologies $8,900/mo) are sold as 'your AI department'. For a 5-200 staff NJ business, that is a budget-holder decision; the $750-$2,500 band is an owner or office-manager decision and closes faster.

[Inference] Expect price comparison against Upwork, and price the difference explicitly. Reasoning: US automation freelancers advertise a median $80/hr and a worldwide median of $35/hr, so a client can always find a cheaper build. The defensible line is the published-vendor pattern of 30-day fix windows, accounts in the client's name, monitoring and cancellation-with-handover - deliverables a marketplace freelancer rarely documents.

[Inference] A take-it-or-leave-it public price list is itself a differentiator in this segment. Reasoning: AgenticIndex found 85 of 290 agencies (29%) publish no price at all, and 205 that do skew toward small entry tiers. Publishing a pilot price, a build band and a retainer band - as TwoCore, Agentomte, NJ AI Automation and Nyza do - removes the discovery-call gate that buyers complain about.
caveats: All prices were read on 2026-11-12 from the linked pages unless the page itself states an earlier date (SuperDupr 'as of October 2026'; Agentomte 'current as of July 2026'; AI Strike Force's 14-agency table 'checked on 23 October 2026').
Many of the vendors that publish clean prices are small or solo operations. Their published prices are real list prices, but they are not evidence of what a 50-person New Jersey company negotiates.

Two agency comparison sources used here (AI Strike Force's 14-agency table and AgenticIndex's 290-agency report) are compiled by parties with a commercial interest in the category; the individual figures they attribute to other agencies were not all re-opened at source by me.

Reddit, Indie Hackers, Trustpilot and Clutch blocked direct retrieval (HTTP 403 or JavaScript-only). Complaint and Clutch figures in this file therefore come from thread titles/listing metadata as returned in search results, not from the page body; they should be treated as directional.
Vendor case studies (Streamline IQ) and third-party write-ups (Wealthy Tent) report seller-side prices and buyer outcomes supplied by the seller; no invoice, contract or buyer confirmation was seen.
Published entry prices are often the smallest possible scope. Where a vendor publishes a band ('$1,500-$5,000'), the band is reproduced as published and no midpoint should be treated as a quote.
data_gaps: No New Jersey or Middlesex County agency published a full rate card with tiers, overage and cancellation terms; the closest local data are NJ AI Automation (audit/build/support only) and The Automators (Calgary-based, markets to NJ, $125/hr).

No independent survey of what small US businesses actually pay AI automation agencies was found. The AgenticIndex and AI Services Companies datasets are analyses of published prices and self-reported firm data, not invoices.
Cancellation and refund terms are unstated by most vendors, including Dominion (explicitly), MapScale, AutomateNexus, SuperDupr and AI Strike Force.

No public hourly rate was found for the NJ/NYC agencies that serve Middlesex County; only The Automators ($125/hr USD), OVAMIND ($250/hr launch), XRAY ($250/hr, via third-party) and Upwork marketplace medians.

Free trials were not found at any agency in this set; the closest equivalents are conditional refunds (Agentomte audit refund, Automaly assessment refund) and free 20-30 minute consultations (MapScale, SuperDupr, AI Strike Force, The Automators, AutomateNexus).

Buyer-side complaint evidence is thin because review platforms (Clutch, Trustpilot, Capterra) and forums (Reddit, Indie Hackers) blocked retrieval; the four complaints listed are directional and should be re-checked manually before use in a proposal.
